title: Measuring Advance Money for Return on a Car Rental
content:
On a Car Rental Rate Classes rental, what the money settled in advance is taken as, for the purpose of
returning it, depends on the currency it was collected in and on the number of payments it came in. The
currency the supplier publishes is US dollars.

**Where the money settled in advance was collected in a currency other than the one the supplier publishes**,
it is taken as what was collected less the rate class's currency conversion markup, at the markup published
by the rate class booked.

**Where the money settled in advance was collected in the supplier's own currency in more than one payment**,
it is taken as the largest single payment collected.

**Where neither holds**, it is taken as the whole of what was collected.

## Which case answers

The first case turns on the currency alone and the second on the count of payments alone, and the first is
reached first: money collected in another currency is measured by the markup even where it came in several
payments.

More than one payment means two or more advance payments standing on the rental. Where the money came in a
single payment in the supplier's own currency, neither case is reached.

## Two measures worked through

A rental carrying advance payments of 640 USD collected in a currency other than US dollars, on a class
whose currency conversion markup is 3 per cent: the money settled in advance is taken as 640 USD less 3 per
cent of it, which is 620.80 USD.

A rental carrying three advance payments in US dollars of 200 USD, 350 USD and 120 USD: the money settled in
advance is taken as 350 USD, the largest single payment collected.
